This R markdown script demonstrates the practical use of our proposed helper functions to estimate incremental costs between two groups in a realistic dataset.

- **`glmx()`** fits multiple regression models using three different packages (`stats::glm(), glm2::glm2(), glmmTMB::glmmTMB()`) and returns the best fitting model.
- **`glmx_events()`** fits multiple regression models for the first stage of a two stage model (number of events with non-zero costs) using Poisson with identity and log-link, and returns the best fitting model.
- **`glmx_pcosts()`** fits multiple regression models for the second stage of a two stage model (positive costs) using Gamma with identity and log-link, and returns the best fitting model.
- **`glmx_best_model()`** returns the model with the lowest AIC from all converged models (non-NULL, converged, and valid AIC).
- **`marginal_one_stage()`** predicts marginal cost difference between groups for a single stage model based on a population sample (here, the study sample).
- **`marginal_two_stage()`** predicts marginal cost difference between groups for a two stage model based on a population sample (here, the study sample).

## Setup and Libraries

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
  N_sim  <-  1000 # should be at least  1000
  N_boot <- 10000 # should be at least 10000

  # source, intermediate, and target files
  meps2024_remote <- "https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_files/pufs/h256/h256xlsx.zip"
  meps2024_local  <- "./h256.xlsx"
  placebo_results <- "./Placebo_MEPS.Rdata"

  # required libraries
  library(tidyverse)
  library(flextable)
  library(readxl)
  library(mgcv)
  library(glm2)
  library(glmmTMB)
  library(foreach)
  library(doParallel)
  library(RhpcBLASctl)
  library(marginaleffects)

  # set chunk defaults, prepare to analyze simulations in parallel (no random numbers)
  knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.0, dpi = 600, comment = NA)
  registerDoParallel(min(4, get_num_cores())); blas_set_num_threads(min(4, get_num_cores()))

  # utility function to plot in high resolution to *.png and *.pdf file and inline
  plot_pdf_png <- function(file_name, aspect_ratio, plot_object, plot_width = 6.0, plot_res = 600) {
    themed_object <- plot_object + theme(text = element_text(size = 10), plot.title = element_text(size = 10))
    png(sprintf("%s.png", file_name), width = plot_width, height = plot_width * aspect_ratio, units = "in", res = plot_res); print(themed_object); ignore <- dev.off()
    pdf(sprintf("%s.pdf", file_name), width = plot_width, height = plot_width * aspect_ratio, paper = "a4");                 print(themed_object); ignore <- dev.off()
    knitr::include_graphics(sprintf("%s.png", file_name))
  }
```

## Robust Regressions

Infrastructure and utility functions (skip ahead to dataset)

```{r robust_regressions}
  # utility function to select best regression fit, instrumented to track performance
  glmx_best_model <- function(m_list) {
    returned  <- map_lgl(m_list,  ~       !is.null(.x))
    converged <- map_lgl(m_list,  ~ifelse(!is.null(.x),   class(.x)[1] == "lm" || (class(.x)[1] == "glm" && .x$converged[1]) || (class(.x)[1] == "glmmTMB" && .x$fit$convergence == 0), FALSE))
    AICs      <- map_dbl(m_list,  ~ifelse(!is.null(.x) & (class(.x)[1] == "lm" || (class(.x)[1] == "glm" && .x$converged[1]) || (class(.x)[1] == "glmmTMB" && .x$fit$convergence == 0)), AIC(.x), NA))
    valid_AIC <- !is.na(AICs)
    if (sum(valid_AIC) == 0) { return(NULL) }
    best_AIC <- which.min(AICs) # which.min ignores NA and NaN
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$returned  <- returned
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$converged <- converged
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$valid_AIC <- valid_AIC
    m_list[[best_AIC]]$best_AIC  <- ifelse(!is.na(AICs), AICs == min(AICs, na.rm = TRUE), FALSE)
    return(m_list[[best_AIC]])
  }

  # wrapper function around glm, glm2::glm2, and glmmTMB::glmmTMB, selecting the best among multiple fits
  # ML (not REML) is required for AIC comparisons across packages, to ensure comparable likelihood estimation
  # lm() provides starting values to overcome glm/glm2 error "no valid set of coefficients has been found: please supply starting values"
  # non-ML gam() provides an alternative set of starting values for glmmTMB()
  glmx <- function(formula, data, family) {
    s2 <- coef(gam(formula, family, data)) # default (non-ML) mgcv::gam() returns reliably
    s1 <- s2                               # copy names of predictors as lm() may silently remove some
    s1[which(names(s1) != "(Intercept)")] <- 0.0
    s1[which(names(s1) == "(Intercept)")] <- mean(predict(lm(formula, data), type = "response"))
    if (family$link == "log") s1[which(names(s1) == "(Intercept)")] <- log(s1[which(names(s1) == "(Intercept)")])
    models <- list(NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL)
    try(models[[1]] <-     glm(formula, family, data, start = s1))
    try(models[[2]] <-    glm2(formula, family, data, start = s1))
    try(models[[3]] <- glmmTMB(formula, data, family,                          REML = FALSE, na.action = na.exclude))
    try(models[[4]] <- glmmTMB(formula, data, family, start = list(beta = s1), REML = FALSE, na.action = na.exclude))
    try(models[[5]] <- glmmTMB(formula, data, family, start = list(beta = s2), REML = FALSE, na.action = na.exclude))
    return(glmx_best_model(models))
  }

  # wrapper to select the best fit among poisson, the latter with identity link or log-link, for counts
  glmx_events <- function(formula, data) {
    models <- list(NULL, NULL)
    try(models[[1]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = poisson(link = "identity")))
    try(models[[2]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = poisson(link = "log")))
    return(glmx_best_model(models))
  }

  # wrapper to select the best fit among gamma regressions with identity link or log-link, for positive costs
  glmx_pcosts <- function(formula, data) {
    models <- list(NULL, NULL)
    try(models[[1]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = Gamma(link = "identity")))
    try(models[[2]] <- glmx(formula, data, family = Gamma(link = "log")))
    return(glmx_best_model(models))
  }

  # utility function to extract marginal cost difference for single stage model evaluated on target population (can be the study population)
  marginal_one_stage <- function(pop, m1, model) {
    costdiff <- NA
    try(costdiff <- mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response")) -
                    mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response")))
    return(data.frame(costdiff, model))
  }

  # utility function to extract marginal cost difference for Gaussian/Poisson-Gamma model evaluated on target population (can be the study population)
  marginal_two_stage <- function(pop, m1, m2, model) {
    costdiff <- NA
    try(costdiff <- mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response") * predict(m2, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "intervention"), type = "response")) -
                    mean(predict(m1, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response") * predict(m2, newdata = pop %>% mutate(study_group = "control"),      type = "response")))
    return(data.frame(costdiff, model))
  }
```

## Real-World Dataset

**Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality**

- Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS) https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/ for 2024
- Variables: IPDIS (number of inpatient hospital discharges), IPFTCH (inpatient hospital charges), INSCOV (insurance status), POVCAT (income category), DATAYEAR, AGELAST, SEX, and BORNUSA
- No weighting is performed
- MEPS codes missing values as negative numbers, and any such records are excluded
- Only records with (0 costs and 0 stays) or with (positive stays and positive costs) are included
- Costs are shifted by +0.01 USD for Gaussian(log) and Gamma regressions (pcost)
- Costs per event (ecost) are defined as the cost per inpatient discharge, and they are used as the outcome of the second stage of the two-stage model

```{r dataset}
  if (!file.exists(meps2024_local)) {
    temp_file <- tempfile(); download.file(meps2024_remote, temp_file, method = "auto"); unzip(temp_file, overwrite = TRUE, junkpaths = TRUE); unlink(temp_file)
  }
  study_pop <- read_xlsx(meps2024_local) %>%
    select(N = matches("^IPDIS"), cost = matches("^IPFTCH"), INSURANCE = matches("^INSCOV"), INCOME = matches("^POVCAT"), DATAYEAR, AGELAST, SEX, BORNUSA) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(.x < 0, NA, .x))) %>% filter(AGELAST >= 18)
  print(sprintf("MEPS %s: Adults, Obs. = %d, Complete = %d (used, assuming MCAR)", paste(unique(study_pop$DATAYEAR), collapse = ", "), nrow(study_pop), nrow(study_pop %>% filter(complete.cases(.)))))
  study_pop <- study_pop %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
  print(sprintf("Removed = %d because !((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0))", nrow(study_pop %>% filter(!((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0))))))
  study_pop <- study_pop %>% filter((N == 0 & cost == 0.0) | (N > 0 & cost > 0.0)) %>%
    mutate(SEX       = factor(SEX,       levels = 1:2, labels = c("Male", "Female"))) %>%
    mutate(INSURANCE = factor(INSURANCE, levels = 1:3, labels = c("1: Private", "2: Public", "3: Uninsured"))) %>%
    mutate(INCOME    = factor(INCOME,    levels = 1:5, labels = c("1: Poor", "2: Near poor", "3: Low", "4: Middle", "5: High"))) %>%
    mutate(BORNUSA   = factor(BORNUSA,   levels = 1:2, labels = c("Born in USA", "Born outside USA"))) %>%
    mutate(pcost     = cost + 0.01, ecost = cost / pmax(N, 1)) %>%
    mutate(study_group = ifelse(BORNUSA == "Born in USA", "control", "intervention"))
  study_pop %>% group_by(BORNUSA) %>% reframe(N_Group = n(), Mean_USD = sum(cost) / sum(N), Prop_0_Cost = sprintf("%.01f %%", 100.0 * sum(cost == 0.0) / n())) %>% flextable() %>% autofit()
```

## Placebo Study

We used a "placebo design" with real data: persons were randomly allocated two groups (intervention and control), so that the true cost difference is zero by construction. This follows the logic of placebo analyses (Bertrand et al., 2004; Eggers et al., 2024) and of randomization methods based on repeated random assignment. All regressions are adjusted for age and sex.

```{r placebo, warning = FALSE}
  # placebo allocation, serial not parallel
  set.seed(314159)
  pop_list <- list()
  for (i in 1:N_sim) {
    pop_list[[2*i-1]] <- study_pop %>% slice_sample(n = 2000, replace = FALSE) %>% mutate(study_group = ifelse(runif(nrow(.)) > 0.5, "control", "intervention")) # mimic RCT
    pop_list[[2*i]]   <- study_pop %>%                                             mutate(study_group = ifelse(runif(nrow(.)) > 0.5, "control", "intervention")) # mimic Registry
  }

  # regression model, adjusting for age and sex
  formula1 <- outcome ~ study_group + AGELAST + SEX

  # regressions fits, parallel
  results <- foreach (i = 1:length(pop_list), .combine = rbind, .packages = c("tidyverse", "glm2", "mgcv", "glmmTMB")) %dopar% {
    group_pop <- pop_list[[i]]
  
    # one-stage models: Gaussian (identity), Gaussian (log), Gamma (identity), and Gamma (log)
    m_gauss_id  <-   lm(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome =  cost))
    m_gauss_log <- glmx(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome = pcost), family = gaussian(link = "log"))
    m_gamma_id  <- glmx(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome = pcost), family = Gamma(link = "identity"))
    m_gamma_log <- glmx(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome = pcost), family = Gamma(link = "log"))
      
    # two-stage model: number of discharges times costs per discharge
    m_events <- glmx_events(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome = N))
    m_pcosts <- glmx_pcosts(formula1, data = group_pop %>% rename(outcome = ecost) %>% filter(N > 0))

    # marginal cost differences, evaluated on the study sample
    rbind(marginal_one_stage(group_pop, m_gauss_id,         "Gaussian (identity)"),
          marginal_one_stage(group_pop, m_gauss_log,        "Gaussian (log)"),
          marginal_one_stage(group_pop, m_gamma_id,         "Gamma (identity)"),
          marginal_one_stage(group_pop, m_gamma_log,        "Gamma (log)"),
          marginal_two_stage(group_pop, m_events, m_pcosts, "Two-Stage Poisson-Gamma")) %>% mutate(N = nrow(group_pop))
  }
  save(results, file = placebo_results)
```

## Results

```{r results}
  # ensure reproducibility for bootstrap computations
  set.seed(271828)

  # utility function to compute mean value and estimate its confidence interval from bootstrapping, allowing for NA values
  mean_ci <- function(vec, n_boot = N_boot, alpha = 0.01, digits = 2) {
    v <- vec[!is.na(vec)]
    n <- length(v)
    b <- vector(mode = "double", length = n_boot)
    for (i in 1:n_boot) {
      b[i] <- mean(v[sample(1:n, size = n, replace = TRUE)])
    }
    return(sprintf("%.*f [%.*f; %.*f]", digits, mean(v), digits, quantile(b, 0.5 * alpha), digits, quantile(b, 1.0 - 0.5 * alpha)))
  }

  # utility function to compute root mean squared value and estimate with confidence interval from bootstrapping, allowing for NA values
  rmsq_ci <- function(vec, n_boot = N_boot, alpha = 0.01, digits = 2) {
    v <- vec[!is.na(vec)]
    n <- length(v)
    b <- vector(mode = "double", length = n_boot)
    for (i in 1:n_boot) {
      b[i] <- sqrt(mean(v[sample(1:n, size = n, replace = TRUE)]^2))
    }
    return(sprintf("%.*f [%.*f; %.*f]", digits, sqrt(mean(v*v)), digits, quantile(b, 0.5 * alpha), digits, quantile(b, 1.0 - 0.5 * alpha)))
  }

  # aggregate results
  results %>% mutate(model = fct_inorder(model)) %>%
    group_by(N, Model = model) %>% reframe(Bias = mean_ci(    costdiff),
                                           MAE  = mean_ci(abs(costdiff)),
                                           RMSE = rmsq_ci(    costdiff)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(N, Model), names_to = "Metric") %>% pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = value) %>%
    mutate(Type = ifelse(N != nrow(study_pop), "RCT", "Registry")) %>% select(Type, N, Metric, everything()) %>%
    flextable() %>% set_caption(sprintf("Placebo study (MEPS 2024): Metrics in USD [99%%-CI], N_SIM=%d", N_sim)) %>% autofit() %>% hline(3)
```
